newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU report urges aid for young farmers.
newsitem.headline: EU report urges aid for young farmers.

text.p: Europe's ageing farming population must be rejuvenated by giving more start-up help for young farmers so as to ensure a future food supplies, the European Commission said in a report on Friday.

Only about eight percent of the European Union's 8.5 million farmers are under 35 though their farms are well above the average EU size. More than half the region's farmers are now over 55 with small, uneconomic holdings.
But the report added that it was up to the 15 European Union member states to make greater use of structural and marketing aid measures to assist young people.
"Legislation at EU level is of little use if member state governments do not promote and fully utilise the measures available," Fischler said in a statement.
Fischler added that changes in national inheritance and taxation laws would greatly help young farmers get established.
The report, which will be discussed by EU farm ministers, also suggested that start-up aid and training should be adapted to local conditions and a growing trend of farmers holding several jobs.
Early retirement schemes should be designed to encourage take-over of farms by young people who must also be granted a greater share of milk and other production quotas.
But young farmers, complaining that they had not been consulted, attacked the report as vague and lightweight.
"We are very disappointed. There's nothing in it," Georg Hausler, secretary-general of the European Young Farmers Association, said.
Hausler said young farmers' difficulties were linked to the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) and therefore the EU's responsibility.
